72033.subject: Physics
72033.question_text: A stone of mass 200 g attached to a string is made to revolve in a horizontal circle of radius 1.5 m at a steady speed of 5 m/s. Calculate the tension in the string at the bottom of the circle.
72033.explanation:
F\(_c\) = \(\frac{mv^2}{r}\)

mass = 200g = 0.2kg, v = 5 m/s, r = 1.5 m 

F\(_c\) = \(\frac{0.2 \times 5 \times 5}{1.5}\) ≈ 3.33N

At the bottom of the circle, the tension T in the string must counteract the weight of the stone as well as provide the centripetal force:

T = F\(_c\) + mg

T = 3.33 + 0.2 x 10 = 5.3N

72041.subject: Physics
72041.question_text:
A cube of water with side 10.0 cm floats vertically in water with 4.5 cm its length submerged. Calculate the density of the wood.
[Density of water = 1 g/cm\(^3\); D = 0.090 g/cm\(^3\)]
72041.explanation:
Volume of cube = s\(^3\) = 10\(^3\) = 1000cm\(^3\)

Volume of cube submerged = 10 cm x 10 cm x 4.5 cm = 450 cm\(^3\)

Volume of water displaced = volume of cube submerged = 450 cm\(^3\)

Mass of water displaced = 1 cm\(^3\) x 450 cm\(^3\) = 450g (density of water is 1 cm\(^3\))

Mass of cube = V\(_{cube}\) x \(\rho_{cube}\)

But, mass of cube = mass of water displaced

1000 cm\(^3\) x \(\rho_{cube}\) = 450g

\(\rho_{cube}\) = \(\frac{450}{1000}\) = 0.45 g/cm\(^3\)

72051.subject: Physics
72051.question_text: A particle of mass 3.6 x 10\(^{-6}\)kg revolving around the earth has a radial acceleration of 4.3 x 10\(^7\)ms\(^{-2}\). Calculate the centripetal force of the particle.
72051.explanation:

F\(_c\) = m x a\(_c\) = 3.6 x 10\(^{-6}\) x 4.3 x 10\(^7\) = 154.8N ≈ 155N ⇒ 1.55 x 10\(^2\)N

72057.subject: Physics
72057.question_text: A body of mass, m is projected vertically upward with a velocity, y. At what position will the potential energy be maximum?
72057.explanation:
At the maximum height, all the kinetic energy will have been converted into potential energy:

mgh = \(\frac{1}{2}\)mv\(^2\)

v = y

gh = \(\frac{1}{2}\)y\(^2\)

h = \(\frac{y^2}{2g}\)

Thus, the potential energy will be maximum at the height given by: \(\frac{y^2}{2g}\)

72061.subject: Physics
72061.question_text: A boy of mass 40 kg jumps off a stationary skateboard and moves horizontally with a speed of 1.5 m/s while the skateboard moves in the opposite direction with a speed of 20 m/s. Calculate the mass of the skateboard.
72061.explanation:
Given: mass of boy = 40 kg = m\(_b\), mass of skateboard = ? = m\(_k\), speed of skateboard v\(_x\) = - 20 m/s, speed of boy v\(_y\) = 1.5 m/s

Both the skateboard and the boy were initially at rest.

The total momentum before and after the jump must be equal.

0 = m\(_b\) x v\(_y\) + m\(_k\) x  v\(_x\)

0 = 40 x 1.5  +  m\(_k\) x (-20)

0 = 60 - 20m\(_k\)

20m\(_k\) = 60

m\(_k\) = \(\frac{60}{20}\) = 3 kg.

72075.subject: Physics
72075.question_text: A non-conducting vessel contains a liquid of mass 70 g at 25º C. Another 70.0g of the same liquid at 35ºC is quickly poured into the vessel. Determine the final temperature of the mixture
72075.explanation:
Heat gained by 25º C body = Heat lost by 35º C body

M\(_c\) c \(\delta\)\(\theta\) = M\(_h\) c\(\delta\)\(\theta\)

70 x c x (f - 25) = 70 x c x (35 - f)

where f = final temperature

f - 25 = 35 - f (f and 70 cancel out)

2f = 35 + 25 = 60

f = \(\frac{60}{2}\) = 30ºC

72076.subject: Physics
72076.question_text: A galvanometer of full-scale deflection 10 mA has a resistance of 5\(\Omega\). Calculate the shunt needed to convert it to measure currents of 2 A.
72076.explanation:
Voltage across shunt = Voltage across galvanometer

I\(_s\)R\(_s\) = I\(_g\)R\(_g\)

R\(_g\) = 5\(\Omega\),  I\(_g\) = 10mA = 0.01A, I\(_s\) = 2 - 0.01 = 1.99A

R\(_s\) = \(\frac{I_g \times R_g}{I_s}\) = \(\frac{0 .01 \times 5}{1.99}\) = 0.025\(\Omega\)
